what_it_is: Root assets: app/favicon icons, share card, chest parts, harvest basket layers, soil, tufts and harvest FX sprites.
biggest_problem: Chest set carries a baked cream sticker halo (Hearthlight fallback) that reads as a thick white ring on dark felt, unlike its halo-free basket and tuft siblings. harvest-basket-back is a hollow white/transparent blob with a thin outline that looks like a stand-in.

harvest-puff: faint pale specks, nearly invisible on cream paper
icon-16: gnome badge muddy at 16 px, hat-only silhouette needed
strengths: Gnome hat icon family is consistent across 16-512 with umber outline and warm palette. Woven baskets, fruit heap and three harvest tufts are crisp pixel art with upper-left light and match Stitched Toy well; spark FX reads on both themes.

what_it_is: Framed activity vignettes (still plus 6-frame anim strip) of a gnome doing each act, regional variants
biggest_problem: A handful of stills use a different, higher-detail gnome (bigger, smoother shading, softer edges) that breaks the tiny-gnome family. Sheets downscale ~120 tiles each, so anim strips and outline colour cannot be verified; frame-level checks need closer sheets.

what_it_is: Activity vignette cards (still plus 6-frame anim strip per act, worlds w1-w5 and regional r_*) plus badge, felt and ribbon UI pieces
biggest_problem: A few snow scenes use a large, detailed bearded gnome off-model from the tiny standard gnome. Anim strips are too small on the sheets to check frame-to-frame motion or confirm the frame counts. Many vignettes are near-identical "gnome next to a prop" compositions, and the prop is hard to read at card size.
outliers: act-w2_ice_paddles: oversized detailed gnome, off-model
act-w3_snowy_lanterns: oversized detailed gnome, off-model
act-w4_frost_pots: oversized detailed gnome, off-model
act-r_ea_snow_monkeys: oversized gnome, unlike siblings

badge-done: rounded octagon/circle UI shape

act-w3_croft_bees: baked tally-mark text on board
strengths: The family is very consistent: the same wooden frame, umber outlines, warm palette and a gnome shape that is the same nearly everywhere. Strips and stills match one-to-one. Dark-theme cards sit cleanly on the felt with no halos. Time-of-day palettes add variety, and the felt and ribbon UI pieces have crisp pixel edges.

what_it_is: Animal characters, their housing/buildings, and animal-derived item drops (eggs, silk, feathers, scutes).
biggest_problem: The heavy dark sticker border and drop shadow nearly vanish on dark felt, so silhouettes flatten there. A few tiles break the family look: goat is thin and pale, tortoise_run is a busy scene, and eggs and cocoons blur together. I could only see the sheets at a scale where exact outline hex and halo pixels weren't clear.
outliers: goat: spindly legs, pale body, weak silhouette, lighter outline than siblings
tortoise_run: busy mini-scene with a baked-in extra creature; unreadable at icon size
item-goat-hair: vague white tufts, no clear read

item-scute-wind-chime: cluttered, small parts mush at 24-36 px
strengths: The set is complete and coherent. Outlines are warm umber, shading is warm and lit from the upper left, and creatures have felt-style eyes. Butterfly, frog, hen, snail, ladybird, tortoise and worm have strong silhouettes that match the pilot. No placeholders and no baked-in text.

what_it_is: Catfish minigame: layered cat paper-doll parts (patterns, ears, eyes, tails, masks), room2 furniture/backdrop layers, lure/wand FX, upgrade and yarn icons.
biggest_problem: Room2 layers are uneven: bird is a chunky, oversized low-res lump; window, window-nobird, p4-front and p5b-night look almost empty. Many eye frames are blank. Room2 cat strip sheets are too small to judge frame detail. Black calico ears and patches disappear on dark felt.

what_it_is: Catfish cat-cafe minigame: layered cat sprites (base poses plus ear, eye, collar, pattern overlays), badges, pet decor, regional banners, room pieces.
biggest_problem: Base cats use a thick dark sticker rim that nearly vanishes on dark felt, and badges are round medallions (circles banned in UI art). Overlay layers cannot be judged alone: many eye frames are blank, tuxedo patterns are faint ghosts, and the room and season bits are too tiny to read on the sheet.
outliers: cf-badge-book_full: round medallion UI shape
cf-badge-legendary: circular badge, busy at small size
cf-bookhead-unknown: '?' glyph stand-in

cf-pet-mask_frame: framed human face portrait
strengths: Base cat set is excellent: 8 coats x ~20 poses with a shared anchor, size, palette ramp and upper-left light. Felt-stitch highlights, clear silhouettes, and each pose reads well. Pet decor icons are charming and consistent, and the regional banners are rich, cohesive pixel scenes.

what_it_is: Crafting-station backdrop scenes (building, cooking, decor, garden, pantry, potions, tools), each with a -t twin
biggest_problem: Decor scenes bake in a robin, which breaks the no-animals rule for backdrops. Building, tools and potions use soft radial glow halos that clash with the hard-pixel rule. Each -t twin looks the same as its base at sheet scale, so the pairs may be redundant. There is no dark sheet, so dark-theme fit was not checked.
outliers: decor: baked-in robin on birdbath (animal in backdrop)
decor-t: same baked-in robin

potions: soft teal glow behind cauldron
cooking: near-black stove reads harsher than umber palette
strengths: The set is strong and coherent. Every scene has the same framing: a shelf rail at the top, a plank floor and props at the same scale. The pixel props read clearly, light comes from the upper left, the palette is warm and there is no baked-in text. Each station is easy to tell apart at a glance.

what_it_is: Ground-cover autotile sets (clover, dirt, dry, flowers, leaves, moss, weeds; 47 blob tiles each) plus 6 lawn tuft decals.
biggest_problem: Dirt and leaves edges vanish on dark felt: no umber rim or lip, so the shape disappears into the background. Clover and flowers are a bit too saturated for the warm, low-contrast palette. Stray dark pinhole pixels sit near the notched edges in dark mode. Sheet 03 (moss, weeds) has no dark twin, so those sets were not checked on dark.
outliers: dirt-0: notched edge merges into dark felt, no rim
leaves-0: edge vanishes on dark theme
leaves-95: looks warmer and more saturated than its leaves siblings

flowers-12: dark speck pixels near top-right notch
clover-1: stray dark pixel near right edge on dark
lawn-1: very sparse, reads as near-empty at game size
clover-0: bright saturated green, off the warm palette
strengths: All 7 sets have the full 47-tile blob, with the same size, anchor and texture placement. Edges are crisp hard pixels with no AA halos. Textures are pleasant and dithered, with readable flower and leaf flecks. The lawn tufts are charming felt-like decals.

what_it_is: Autotile path families (logs, pots, steps, toads) in big/medium/small sizes, with end, straight, corner, tee, cross and curve variants.
biggest_problem: The toads family is flat red-and-white with a near-black outline, not felt shading, so it clashes with logs and pots. Steps have stray wedge slivers and fuzzy seams where stones meet. Small steps read as specks. There is no dark sheet for page 3, so toads and small steps are unchecked on felt.
outliers: toads-b-1: flat glossy cap, near-black outline, off-style versus logs and pots

logs-b-a0: bottom log cut off at the tile edge
strengths: Logs and pots are strong. Each has a warm palette, a clean umber outline, a soft drop shadow and a full 32-variant set across all three sizes. Light falls consistently from the upper left. Logs and pots also read well on dark felt with no halos.

what_it_is: Battle sprite rig atlases: per-creature body-part sheets plus outline/mask silhouettes, and a demo gnome walk strip.
biggest_problem: Atlases are mostly tiny generic part sets reused across species (same leg/torso/head shapes recoloured), so creatures lack their own silhouettes; several use geometric stand-ins or off-style art. Parts are too small on the sheet to judge felt shading in detail. Outline-mask rows (#2b1c26) disappear on dark felt.

what_it_is: Flower, foliage sprig and container icons (bouquet/arranging items), 19 PNGs with SVG twins.
biggest_problem: 18 of 19 PNGs have an outermost 1px ring of pure black (#000000) outside the umber band; only basket is clean. On dark felt this reads as a heavy black sticker border. Canvas sizes also vary (64x64, 64x96 sprigs, 200x150 basket/jar).

strengths: Cohesive warm palette, hard pixel edges with no semi-transparent halos, clear upper-left light and lower-right shade. Flower heads (daisy, poppy, sunflower, tulip, rose, orchid) have strong distinct silhouettes and sit well on both cream and dark felt. No blanks or stand-ins.

what_it_is: Layered bouquet parts: grey tintable petal layers, centre overlays, composites, sprigs, and basket, jar, vase and packet containers.
biggest_problem: On dark felt the umber outline almost disappears, so the grey petal layers lose their edges. packet has a soft cream halo, which is Hearthlight-style. rose-centre is an empty outline that reads as a placeholder. Several centre overlays are sparse dots that are hard to read alone.

strengths: Consistent umber outline, hard pixel edges and upper-left light on most petals. The layer system (petals, centre, composite) is clean and tintable. The basket, jar and vase containers are charming and on-style. The sprigs read well, and all 46 files are present with no baked-in text.

what_it_is: Small battle/idle effects: shadow, heal/hit/snack strips, KO sparkles, shield bubble, steam puffs, sleep Zs.
biggest_problem: Fx-shield is a thin smooth-looking circle ring that reads as generic vector UI, not felt pixel art. Ground-shadow is fully opaque brown, so it nearly disappears on the dark felt. Steam uses a grey-lavender edge, not umber. Snack frames are specks that are hard to read at game size.

what_it_is: Garden folk NPCs: 11 critter icons, 63 bust portraits, and 63 four-frame walk sprites (21 species x 3 variants).
biggest_problem: Every portrait sits on a coloured circle disc, which breaks the no-circles rule and reads as a generic avatar badge. The firefly folk designs are also confusing: an orange cyclops dome over a dark faceless lump reads as a mushroom, not a firefly.

The sprite sets all have four frames at a consistent scale. The critter icons are clean and readable on both themes, with no halos on the dark felt.

what_it_is: Gathering minigame art: badges, felt tiles, ribbons, rarity flourishes, satchel layers, scene backdrops (old and scene3 day/dusk/night), tool slots, vignettes, weather overlays.
biggest_problem: Two backdrop generations coexist: old scene-* bake in the satchel plus animals (gull, heron, birds), breaking the no-creatures rule and clashing with clean scene3 set. weather-cloud reads blank; satchel-front is a plain stand-in lump; circular badges break no-circles UI rule.

what_it_is: Minigame pieces: five crop pickups, a mail envelope, and five colour-variant racing snails (64px PNG with SVG twins).
biggest_problem: Snails mostly lack the 1px umber outline that the crops have, so their bodies and shells blur into the dark felt. They also face different ways (gold and grey face left, the rest face right), and a few have stray purple or blue fringe pixels and their own different shadow strips.

All PNGs have hard alpha and no pure black. The envelope has no baked-in text and reads instantly. The snail colour variants are easy to tell apart and charming.

what_it_is: Layered paper-doll parts (80x100 shared canvas) composited into the player gnome: hat, band, star, face, beard, scarf, body, shadow.
biggest_problem: Grey tint-mask layers (hat, beard, scarf) use grey outlines, not umber #2a1a10, so after runtime tinting the outline shifts colour and clashes with umber-outlined body, face and band. The scarf layer reads as robotic arm/pipe pieces, not a knitted scarf. No idle/animation frames exist.

strengths: Assembled gnome is charming with a clear silhouette. Hard pixel edges, no partial alpha. Body and face use the correct umber outline and stitched dashes. All layers share one canvas and anchor. Reads well on both cream and dark felt with no halos.

what_it_is: Garden-yard buildings: empty BUILD plots, three build levels, 4-frame ready/reward strips per building, plus fence and ground backdrop.
biggest_problem: Inconsistent building footprints across sets. Kitchen, ladybird, tortoise_run and worm_farm sit on brown dirt slabs and others float. Building scale jumps between sets. Every -e plot has baked-in "BUILD" text. On the 1512px sheet I could not confirm outline hex values at pixel level.

what_it_is: 310 item, UI and concept icons (ico-*, plus pk-* puzzle bits and wander-* trail badges) used in menus, puzzles and rewards.
biggest_problem: The core set is strong, but a few subsets drift. The wander-* round badges break the no-circles UI rule and use a thicker, more saturated style. The four kettles are undersized, low-detail lumps. Sheet 03 has no dark twin, so 100+ icons, wander-* included, were not checked on felt.

what_it_is: Rarity gems, felt card backs, window frames, ribbons, badges, petal and sparkle strips for items/rewards UI
biggest_problem: Rarity gems bake in letters (C/L/R/U) against the no-text rule, and gem-c is a round coin, breaking the no-circle rule. Gems also differ in canvas size (26, 28, 26x28, 32). On dark felt the #2a1a10 outlines nearly vanish, so shapes lose their edge.

Felt tiles and ribbons have a clean stitched texture, upper-left light and a consistent palette. Set sizes within felt, rib and win stay consistent. The petal and the badge-use ticket read well.

what_it_is: Jigsaw puzzle pictures: 14 regional scenes (each with a thumb) plus about 81 delve/haven/lair/wonder place scenes
biggest_problem: The two families split. The region scenes are dense hidden-object pixel art. The places are flatter and reuse one wavy gradient-sky template. Some places look vector-flat or blobby rather than felt-and-stitch. The sheets are too small to check the umber outline or edges. No dark sheets were supplied.

The lair and wonder places have strong centred subjects that work well as puzzles. The region scenes are richly detailed, fit for jigsaws, and show no baked-in text.

what_it_is: Marketing landing-page art: 7 feature illustrations (almanac, cook, games, garden, hero, roads, stats) plus 12 light/dark app screenshots.
biggest_problem: Screenshot pairs are unreliable: shot-town and shot-world "light" versions are dark-theme captures, near-identical to their -dark twins, so the light/dark story breaks. Illustrations also mix frames: hero has no card border and a shorter aspect, cook has rounded corners, others use square dashed cards.

Screenshots look current and show real UI. The art reads well on both cream and dark felt with no visible halos.

what_it_is: 14 journal region stamp medallions (96x96), one per world region, each with a landmark plus a native animal.
biggest_problem: Every badge is a round medallion, which breaks the no-circles rule for UI art. The outline is plum #2b1c26, not umber #2a1a10. Animals are cropped by the rim in a few badges. On dark felt, the outer dark outline blends into the background, so only the coloured ring defines the edge.

what_it_is: World-map art: five 16px felt difficulty terrain tiles, a 240px embroidery-hoop map frame, four difficulty landmarks and a 16px location pin.
biggest_problem: All four landmarks and the pin use pure #000000 pixels (30-52 each) in a heavy outer outline/drop shadow next to umber. The outline reads too heavy and black, and on dark felt it merges into the background. landmark-hard is a grey lump that is hard to read at 16px.

what_it_is: 72 dock and navigation button icons (dock-*) for the bottom bar and action menus
biggest_problem: On dark felt, the umber outline blends into the background, so the silhouettes lose their edges. dock-sneak is almost invisible: only the eyes and feet show. Thin icons (hunt, fight, tools, till, sit) thin out too. Icons with no rim need a light keyline or a felt backing chip.

strengths: Hard pixel edges, umber outline rather than black, a warm palette and consistent upper-left lighting. Strong icons: heal, house (hovel), you, garden, satchel, festival, snack, almanac and tog. They sit well on cream and share a grid and scale.

what_it_is: Mini map/encounter sprites: ~140 critters and bosses, ~60 gnome NPC minis, and gnome paper-doll layer parts.
biggest_problem: Creature scale is erratic: some critters (barn-rat, earwig, dung-beetle, stag-beetle-patrol, page-silverfish) are tiny slivers next to oversized ones, hurting silhouette at game size. The grey ground shadow reads as a pale smudge on dark felt. Gnome layer parts look like blank stand-ins when shown alone.

what_it_is: 47-variant blob autotile sets for path materials (bark, brick, gravel, stone) plus one stones prop, 189 files.
biggest_problem: Edge masks are raw noisy cut-outs with no umber edge line, and stray hole blobs sit inside tiles. Bark is dark brown on dark felt, so its edges disappear in the dark theme. Edge treatment differs by material: brick is cut clean, stone is dithered and ragged, and gravel has sand fringes.

strengths: The set is complete: all four materials have 47 variants each. Palettes are warm and match within each material. Brick herringbone and gravel pebbles read well, with lighting from the upper left. Stone flags have a clear umber outline that fits Stitched Toy.

what_it_is: NPC walk-cycle strips (8 frames, 64x80 each) for 42 critters and gnomes, in back, front and side views
biggest_problem: The outline is plum #2b1c26, not umber #2a1a10. On dark felt it almost matches the background, so dark-bodied characters (firefly, butterfly, mole, ladybird-front, scarecrow) lose their edges. A few insect designs read as objects instead of creatures. The felt eyes are less clear than in the spicepeak pilot.

The gnome cast and critters like the squirrel, snail, frog, beaver and wren have warm, charming silhouettes and readable walk cycles.

what_it_is: Puzzle-fight UI kit: jigsaw piece tiles and edges, sockets, move icons, combo badges, mod/tag marks, fx strips, overlays and debug masks
biggest_problem: Mixed families: soft painted ico-* move icons (bash, jab, lull, roll) sit beside bold haloed stickers (heal, guard, charm). Dark umber foe edge outlines vanish on dark felt. Black-and-red debug masks, pink hatch patterns and baked digits ship in the game folders. Rounded overlay and frame rects break the no-rounded-UI rule.
outliers: edge-hand-foe-body-body: umber dashed outline nearly invisible on dark sheet (whole edge-*-foe set)

digits-hand: baked-in text glyphs, soft blurry edges
strengths: The piece-hand and piece-strip tiles match well: same pattern per colour, crisp umber outlines, matching socket shapes. Mod, tag and rarity marks are crisp, readable and on-palette. The combo badges (ambush, riposte, win-over) are strong, clear silhouettes with felt stitching.

what_it_is: Puzzle-fight UI: mod/tag/rarity marks, pop headers, jigsaw piece strips, tiles and sockets, plus hundreds of creature move icons (ico-*)
biggest_problem: Creature icons use a saturated four-hue palette swap (orange, blue, yellow, teal) and a soft cream halo around the pixel art. That reads as Hearthlight sticker style, not warm felt. Dark sheets show only pieces and tiles, so creature halos on dark felt go unchecked. The 03-dark sheet is too small to judge the strip pieces closely.

The tag icons on cream cards and the patterned piece strips (one texture per element) are clear and sit well on dark felt.

what_it_is: Puzzle-fight foe move icons (ico-* creature/stat pieces, small+big pairs) plus fight UI parts and mask strips
biggest_problem: The dark sheets don't match the pieces: they show parts and mask strips with pure-black and red debug fills, so the ~1000 icons have no dark-felt check. Their cream halo will probably show as a fringe on felt. The palette rotates the same four saturated hues (orange, yellow, blue, teal), which is harsher than the warm low-contrast target.

what_it_is: Puzzle-fight creature move icons (pieces, tawny-owl to zorilla) plus stat/board strip parts (badges, env tiles, snare, socks, stolen) for the fight UI.
biggest_problem: Every piece icon carries a soft cream halo (Hearthlight-style) that will fringe on dark felt; no dark sheets exist for pieces/stat (the dark sheets given cover parts/marks and parts47 instead). Socks use raw magenta key-colour diamonds that read as placeholders; envtile and frames use rounded corners.

what_it_is: Item, seed-packet, clothing (base/fine/lined), tool, creature-badge, feast, guide-book and region banner icons (a to h)
biggest_problem: Clothing tiers (base, -fine, -lined) are pixel-identical across hundreds of tiles, so they act as stand-ins: players cannot tell tiers apart. About 200 seed packets are near-clones with the same green window. Only sheets 01-02 have dark twins, so dark-theme checks cover just 2 of 10 sheets.

crab-gavel: muddled silhouette at icon size

Hedge and gate tile sets match each other. Food, tools and the broken-tool set read clearly. Banners are clean painted pixel scenes.

what_it_is: Placeholder-tier item icons (crops, seeds, preserves, regional outfits with fine/lined variants), nav icons, NPC portraits, land cards, crop growth stages, buildings
biggest_problem: Seed packets are one recycled template with tiny swatch changes, unreadable as distinct items at 24-36 px. Outfit fine/lined/base variants are pixel-identical, so tiers can't be told apart. NPC portraits use flat vector circles instead of felt pixel art. Dark sheets cover the ca-/cb- files, not this part's files.

Buildings (kitchen-*, root_cellar-*, tailor-*) progress clearly. The dark twins show clean edges with no halos and outlines that hold.

what_it_is: Jigsaw puzzle pictures (still and animated pairs) plus the puzzle cast: Jeff/Ffej mascots, wizard, badges, trophies, banners, win scenes.
biggest_problem: Several puzzle pictures copy recognisable third-party characters and memes (Elmo, Homer, Fry, the blinking-guy meme). That is an IP risk and breaks the cosy garden theme. They also show people as the main subject. blinking-guy is close to a painted portrait, too detailed and high in contrast.

The dark twins hold up with a cream rim and no fringing. Banners and win scenes fit together well. The flower, pig, sunflower, waves and balloons pictures are cosy and on style.

what_it_is: Road event-type icons (beat, chain, fork, riddle, sketch, toll, trade, weather), 96x96 transparent pixel icons
biggest_problem: Five of eight icons carry a pure-black (#000) outer silhouette ring (217-358 edge pixels each) instead of umber #2a1a10; beat, toll and weather use umber. Black reads harsh on cream and merges into dark felt. A recolor pass on the outer outline fixes it.

what_it_is: Inventory item, seed packet, gear (fine/lined/base variants), creature pal, garden tile and building icons, files tamarind to zinnia plus dark-sheet crab to desert
biggest_problem: Set consistency breaks. The tile set mixes flat seamless squares with an isometric block (tile-wild), an oversized tile-turf-big and a rounded tile-bark-path. The tool_shed variants change design and scale. Gear fine/lined/base triplets are nearly identical at icon size. Sheet 21 is very tall and needed crops to read.

Creature pals have felt eyes and clear silhouettes, and their sticker rims hold up on dark felt. Food, jars, hats and backpacks are charming and readable. No baked-in text beyond packet squiggles.

what_it_is: Route/progress map pieces: status pins, felt strip track, thread segments, danger stone/markers, gnome token and goal flag.
biggest_problem: Pixel check: pins, stone, danger markers, gnome-token and goal-flag use pure #000000 outlines (36 to 73 px each). Only the strip and thread pieces use umber. On dark felt, the todo thread (2 to 5 px of brown) and the brown strip edge almost disappear.

what_it_is: Backdrops: region banners, door/house fronts, here-stop/town/stage battle scenes, maps, shops, home/hovel interiors and props, trek strips, craft FX.
biggest_problem: Two looks share the folder. Painted pixel door, here-stop and stage scenes clash with flat vector stop-*, home-* and trek-* scenes. fight-generic is a flat placeholder with baked debug text. trek and wander-step have gnome figures baked in. At this 478-tile scale, I could not check outline colour or fine detail.

what_it_is: Gnome player sprites with grey layer pieces, plus 81 NPC 4-frame walk/idle strips (64x96 frames)
biggest_problem: The gnome set is the outlier. The big-beard and big-hat pieces are flat grey with no outline. Gnome-home uses cold neutral greys (60,60,60), so the main character looks off-palette beside the warm NPCs. On dark felt, thin antenna stalks and dark-robed silhouettes are lost. The shared outline is plum #2b1c26, not umber #2a1a10.

what_it_is: Quest-stage icons (befriend, carry, clear, decorate, feed, gather, haul, light, trial, vigil, wait) shown on step cards
biggest_problem: Two-object compositions (haul, carry, befriend, vigil) get busy and muddy at 24-36 px. On dark felt, the umber outline almost disappears against the brown ground, so brown items (haul planks, basket, hourglass frame) lose their edges. The sheet is small, so I judged fine detail from an upscaled crop.

biggest_problem: Every file has a pure #000000 outer ring (260-720 px each) around the umber #2a1a10 sticker rim, so the umber outline is doubled by a black edge: harsh on cream and it melts into dark felt. Recolour that ring to umber or drop it. Some tier progressions also don't read as one building growing.

what_it_is: Town location/route/shop picture cards in wooden frames, plus three small badge/felt tiles (repair, star, gold felt).

Cave interiors in route-delve and route-lair look like flat near-pure black. badge-repair's dark brown legs vanish on the dark felt.

what_it_is: Trail map: find spots, node marker icons, procedural ground route maps per biome, and placed landmark/props objects.
biggest_problem: The obj landmark set varies in scale, framing and texture: some landmarks use noisy, dithered stone that looks unlike the clean felt shading. Several are flat oval bases or tiny lumps. obj sheets are heavily downscaled (5280px tall), so I could not check fine detail. Ground maps look nearly identical across hundreds of files.

what_it_is: Core UI kit: a round gold button and three tileable felt background swatches (dark, light, umber).
biggest_problem: The button is a circular gold coin, which breaks the no-circles rule for UI art. It also reads as a currency icon, not a pressable control. Its umber outline nearly vanishes on dark felt. It has no pressed or disabled states.

what_it_is: Painted pixel-art village backdrops (160x100) for Honeybrook and Poppyburrow
biggest_problem: Both backdrops bake in characters and animals, breaking the scene rule: a gnome on the bridge, bees and a duck in honeybrook; a cheering gnome, flying hat and birds in poppyburrow. Outline is #2b1c26 (purple-umber), not #2a1a10. Saturated sky blue and greens run cooler and higher-contrast than the warm target. Opaque art, no dark sheet to check.

strengths: Clean hard-edged pixel work with no halos or black. Upper-left sun lighting is consistent. Clear focal landmarks (thatched cottages, hobbit-hole doors). The pair match in size, palette (39 colours) and horizon line. Cosy and readable at game size.

what_it_is: Wearable gear cards: jigsaw-piece frames with a gear icon in a round medallion, cost number, element badge and name banner. 280 files.
biggest_problem: All 280 cards have baked-in text: the name banner and the cost number. The gear sits in a circular medallion, which breaks the no-circles rule.
